THE DIFF (three-dot, against merge-base):
    git diff 77889cc...HEAD -M
Commit list:
    git log 77889cc..HEAD --oneline
One commit: 89ede35 "refactor(#166,#167): make every unit a reachable skill with real argument substitution".

THE SPEC — two GitHub issues on this repo. Fetch the full bodies yourself with:
    gh issue view 166
    gh issue view 167

Their acceptance criteria, quoted so you cannot miss them:

**#166 "The units are unreachable: no frontmatter, so the model never knows ship-create-pr or ship-merge exist"**
- [ ] Every unit is a skill directory with a `SKILL.md`; `commands/` and `skills/` no longer split the plugin
- [ ] Every unit declares a `description` written for the decision it drives — what it does and when to use it, key use case first
- [ ] The ship units stay **model-invocable**. `disable-model-invocation` is not set on them; being reachable is the whole point
- [ ] `description` and `when_to_use` carry the phrases a person actually types — "open a PR", "ship it", "merge this", "close the issue" — so the unit is reached for instead of improvised around
- [ ] Verified by behaviour, not by reading: in a fresh session, "merge PR N" reaches `ship-merge` rather than a bare `gh pr merge`
- [ ] Units taking an argument declare `argument-hint`
- [ ] `allowed-tools` covers the calls each unit actually makes and nothing wider
- [ ] Each `SKILL.md` stays under 500 lines, with reference material in files beside it rather than inlined
- [ ] The names an adopter types are stated, including what the plugin namespace does to them, and the migration doc (#142) carries the change

**#167 "The commands taking an argument use {{input}}, which the platform never substitutes"**
- [ ] All three commands use a substitution the platform actually performs
- [ ] The placeholder sits where the value is read, so the file is honest about where its argument arrives
- [ ] `grep -rn '{{' plugins/ templates/` comes back empty
- [ ] Nothing else in the repo teaches the mustache form — README and the adoption template included

Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding.

**Under 400 words.** Your final message IS the report — no preamble, no offer to help further.

title:	The units are unreachable: no frontmatter, so the model never knows ship-create-pr or ship-merge exist
state:	OPEN
author:	dogkeeper886
labels:	bug, priority:high, refactor
comments:	0
assignees:

--
## What to build

None of the eight commands has YAML frontmatter. Not a missing field — no `---` block at all. Every file opens on its `#` heading.

**What that costs, observed in the field.** Asked to open a PR, the agent opens one: no completeness check, no tests, no code review, no build. Asked to merge, it merges — sometimes deleting the branch, sometimes not, ignoring what the task said, leaving the issue open. It does none of the seven steps `ship-merge` spells out, because it never reaches for `ship-merge` at all. It answers from its own habits.

That is the failure this ticket is about. The units are correct and unreachable.

The platform reads frontmatter to decide four things, and gets none of them from us:

| Field | What it decides | What we get instead |
|---|---|---|
| `description` | what the `/` menu shows, and **what Claude reads to judge whether a unit applies to what the user just asked for** | *"If omitted, uses the first paragraph of markdown content."* Our first paragraph is `## Rules` followed by four `@`-include lines. That is what the model sees when deciding whether anything here is relevant to "merge PR 30" — so it decides nothing is. |
| `when_to_use` | extra trigger phrases, appended to the description | unused. The phrases people actually type — "ship it", "open a PR", "merge this" — are written nowhere. |
| `argument-hint` | autocomplete | nothing — `/ship-create-pr` gives no sign it wants an issue number |
| `allowed-tools` | pre-approves that turn's tools | every `gh` and `git` call in a seven-step command prompts separately |

**`disable-model-invocation` is the trap here, not the fix.** It reads like the safety setting for an irreversible action, and the docs use `/deploy` as its example. But its actual effect is *"Description not in context, full skill loads when you invoke"* — the unit becomes invisible to the model, which produces exactly the freelance merge above. The gate belongs in the unit's body, where it already is, and the unit has to be *found* for that body to matter.

**The form itself has also moved.** `docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/slash-commands` now redirects to the skills page: *"Custom commands have been merged into skills. A file at `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and a skill at `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` both create `/deploy` and work the same way… Skills are recommended since they support additional features."* Our `commands/` half and `skills/` half are the same kind of object, split by history rather than by design.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every unit is a skill directory with a `SKILL.md`; `commands/` and `skills/` no longer split the plugin
- [ ] Every unit declares a `description` written for the decision it drives — what it does and when to use it, key use case first
- [ ] The ship units stay **model-invocable**. `disable-model-invocation` is not set on them; being reachable is the whole point
- [ ] `description` and `when_to_use` carry the phrases a person actually types — "open a PR", "ship it", "merge this", "close the issue" — so the unit is reached for instead of improvised around
- [ ] Verified by behaviour, not by reading: in a fresh session, "merge PR N" reaches `ship-merge` rather than a bare `gh pr merge`
- [ ] Units taking an argument declare `argument-hint`
- [ ] `allowed-tools` covers the calls each unit actually makes and nothing wider
- [ ] Each `SKILL.md` stays under 500 lines, with reference material in files beside it rather than inlined
- [ ] The names an adopter types are stated, including what the plugin namespace does to them, and the migration doc (#142) carries the change

## Blocked by

None, but land #128 first if it is close — otherwise the four QA units get converted and then deleted.

## What to build

Three commands declare their argument with a mustache placeholder:

```
plugins/agent-workflows/commands/ship-create-pr.md:16   Issue number: {{input}}
plugins/agent-workflows/commands/ship-merge.md:16       PR number: {{input}}
plugins/agent-workflows/commands/doc-gen-readme.md:17   Target: {{input}}
```

`{{input}}` is not a substitution the platform performs. The [skills reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) lists `$ARGUMENTS`, `$ARGUMENTS[N]`, `$N`, and named `$name` placeholders declared in an `arguments:` frontmatter field. Nothing mustache-shaped appears anywhere in it — and no unit here uses a real one either: `grep -rn 'ARGUMENTS' plugins/` returns nothing.

The commands work today by accident. From the same page: *"If `$ARGUMENTS` is not present in the content, arguments are appended as `ARGUMENTS: <value>`."* So the issue number does arrive, appended at the end of the prompt, while the line written to carry it stays literally `{{input}}`. The file names a mechanism that does not exist and depends on one it never mentions.

The cost lands downstream. These files are the worked example an adopter copies when writing their own unit, and a unit built on `{{input}}` that does not happen to have the fallback's luck simply ignores what the user typed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three commands use a substitution the platform actually performs
- [ ] The placeholder sits where the value is read, so the file is honest about where its argument arrives
- [ ] `grep -rn '{{' plugins/ templates/` comes back empty
- [ ] Nothing else in the repo teaches the mustache form — README and the adoption template included

## Blocked by

None. Three lines and no design call. If the skill-form move lands first, this rides along with it rather than being done twice.

**Verdict: REVISE** — both issues substantially met; one criterion partially, one over-grant.

**Findings**

| # | sev | location | what's wrong | smallest fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | med | `plugins/agent-workflows/skills/ship-merge/SKILL.md:15-17` | Over-grant. Grants `Bash(git status:*)`, `Bash(git symbolic-ref:*)`, `Bash(git branch --show-current)`; the body instructs none of them (only `gh pr view/checks/merge/comment`, `gh issue view/edit`, `git checkout`, `git pull`, `git branch -d`). Spec: *"`allowed-tools` covers the calls each unit actually makes **and nothing wider**"* | drop the three unused git entries |
| 2 | med | all four SKILL.md | Under-grant. ship-create-pr's body instructs `git switch -c`, `git branch -f`, `git push -u`, `gh pr create`, `gh pr edit`, `gh label create`, `gh issue edit/comment` — none granted; ship-merge omits `gh pr merge/comment`, `gh issue edit`, `git branch -d`; doc-gen-readme grants no `Write`/`Bash` despite "Write README.md" and "render PNG"; doc-review-readme grants no `Edit` despite "on REVISE, edits the README in place". This **violates the "covers" half** of criterion 7 while satisfying "nothing wider". Defensible — the rewritten reviewing-artifacts step 3 argues an irreversible call in `allowed-tools` is "a prompt the human no longer gets" — but that reading is nowhere in #166 | state the read-only-only rule in the units, or add the write calls |
| 3 | low | commit 89ede35 | Spec: *"Verified by behaviour… in a fresh session, 'merge PR N' reaches `ship-merge`"*. No evidence of that run anywhere in the diff or commit body | record the fresh-session check |
| 4 | low | six pre-existing skills | Spec: *"`description` **and `when_to_use`** carry the phrases a person actually types"*. Only the four converted units gained `when_to_use`; reviewing-*/setup/reporting-outcomes have none | add, or scope the criterion to ship/doc units |
| 5 | low | `README.md:84-99` | Heading "Available commands" + a "Commands" column, then a separate "## Skills" section — preserves the very split the change abolished | fold into one table |

**Scope creep — all three extras judged necessary, none creep**

- Code-fence removal: required. With frontmatter above it, the opening ``` would have swallowed each body as a literal code block.
- reviewing-artifacts step 3: required. It previously told reviewers to *delete* `allowed-tools` and treated `commands/` as the user-only mechanism — both directly contradict #166's criteria, so leaving it makes the repo's own review skill fight the change.
- profile-doctrine reword: required. "A command inlines / a skill points" distinguishes nothing once `commands/` is gone; the edit is the minimum restatement.

**Checked** — `grep -rn '{{' plugins/ templates/` empty; all three `$ARGUMENTS` present at the read site; no `commands/` dir remains; every SKILL.md ≤ 222 lines. The #166 body's "eight commands" is stale after #128 — four existed and four were converted; it does not change the assessment.

**Unresolved** — `allowed-tools` is written as a YAML sequence; the docs show a comma-separated string. Worth confirming it parses before trusting the grants.
